answers.why: Balak sees the nation's victories over the Amorites, and Moab fears its numerous people.
Balak asks Balaam to curse the Israelite people confronting Moab.
The innumerable fourth part of Israel refers to the people described in the preceding verse.
Israel is the community with God among them, whom he brought out of Egypt.
The protected Israel is the people whom God brought out of Egypt.
God's deeds concern the same people described as rising like a lion in the next verse.
The Israel whom God blesses is seen in the next verse encamped by tribes.
Balaam sees Israel dwelling according to its tribes.
Balaam praises the tents and dwellings of the encamped nation.
A future ruler arises from Israel to defeat Moab, followed by Israel's national victory.
Israel acts valiantly as Edom and Seir become conquered possessions.
Israel's stay at Shittim is immediately described as the people's involvement with Moabite women.
Israel joining Baalpeor continues the account of the people worshipping Moabite gods.
The LORD's anger falls on the people who joined in Baalpeor worship.
Punishing the people's leaders is intended to turn the LORD's anger away from the nation.
Moses addresses the nation's judges and commands them to punish their men.
The man of Israel is a member of the Israelite community whom Phinehas pursues.
Israel identifies the national membership of the man slain with the woman.
The Israelite slain is identified as Zimri, a leader among the Simeonites.
